body:
Nothing crossed the profitability bar today: the scanner returned zero live arbitrage opportunities across all Kalshi and Polymarket gold contracts. That's a legitimate quiet-day finding, not a sign the scanner is broken — it simply means no combination of legs currently pays more than the fees and slippage they'd cost.

The pricing backdrop explains why. Kalshi's settlement contracts for gold on August 31, 2026 straddle a fair value near $4,340–4,350 (the $4,331.99 strike shows a 0.52/0.54 yes market, tipping to 0.44/0.49 at $4,371.99), which lines up with where spot gold actually sits: gold rose to $4,339.41 per troy ounce on August 19, 2026. That figure caps a sharp bounce — gold was trading at $4,070 an ounce on August 4 — and the move higher tracked spot prices breaching $4,400 per ounce, with futures briefly touching $4,500 as gold held above $4,400 after advancing for two straight sessions on fading Fed rate-hike expectations. It has since chopped around that level, easing back under $4,400 more recently as bond yields climbed.

A few Kalshi year-end strikes look odd on paper — for instance the $4,700 or above contract (bid 0.41) quotes a touch richer than $4,600 or above (bid 0.39), which shouldn't happen since a higher bar is never more likely to be cleared. This isn't free money: both books are thin, quotes go stale between updates, and crossing them in size to actually capture the gap isn't realistic, which is likely why the scanner didn't flag it. Similarly, several far out-of-the-money Kalshi strikes above $4,800 show zero 24-hour volume, so their quoted prices are indicative rather than tradeable. Overall, a calm session: prices are internally consistent with where spot gold has been trading, and no genuine cross-platform edge is currently sitting in the order books.
headline: Gold arbitrage scanner finds zero opportunities as Kalshi prices track spot
